summary: Intermittent 429s during orchestrated worker waves after tenant merge - uneven rate-window smoothing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent 429 throttles observed during scheduled orchestrated worker waves immediately following a tenant merge (two subaccounts merged into NebulaSearch parent org).

Impact:
- Multiple production ingestion jobs returning 429s for ~7-15s bursts, 3-5 times per hour for the last 36 hours.
- Affects downstream ranking pipeline; spikes correlate with orchestrated worker restarts (cron-based parallelizers).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, tenant: nebulasearch-prod, dedicated: no (hosted), models: gptx-13b for text gen and embed-lite-v1 for embeddings.
- Merge occurred 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC (internal tenant consolidation script).

Observed behavior:
- Soft 429s with X-RateLimit-Reason: "window-smoothing-conflict" in headers (internal marker).
- Around the merge time the tenant-level refill window appears to have been switched from 60s smoothing to 300s smoothing, but some route-level token buckets still used the old per-route burst window leading to uneven accounting and short tenant-wide exhausts.

Expected behavior:
- After tenant merge, quota accounting should converge to the configured tenant-level smoothing policy without producing transient 429s for steady workers.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant-merge: consolidate subaccount A and B into parent tenant C (use internal merge tool).
2) Start 50 orchestrated worker processes that each open a short-lived streaming session followed by a burst of concurrent embedding uploads.
3) Observe per-worker success followed by short 429 bursts on ~10% of sessions within first 5 minutes.
4) Inspect rate-limit headers and quota metrics for tenant and routes in console.
logs:
[2026-03-10T00:12:05Z] gateway: request from worker-17 tenant=nebulasearch-prod route=/v1/embeddings status=429 reason=window-smoothing-conflict
[2026-03-10T00:12:06Z] rate-limiter: tenant_token_bucket deplete_estimate=0 refill_window=300s route_token_bucket burst_remaining=0
[2026-03-10T00:12:06Z] ingest-orchestrator: worker-17 retrying after 120ms backoff
[2026-03-10T00:12:20Z] rate-limiter: tenant bucket refill partial=50 tokens
[2026-03-10T00:12:21Z] gateway: worker-17 request status=200 latency=24ms
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed merge ran using consolidation tool v2.1 which flipped default tenant smoothing to 300s window (feature flag: tenant_smoothing_v2).
- Metrics show tenant-level token accounting reports periodic undercounting for ~10s after merge events.
- Route-level buckets for legacy routes retained 60s burst window; the cross-layer refill algorithm double-applies smoothing resulting in tenant tokens being counted then consumed by route refill logic.
- Hypothesis: During merge we left transient in-memory token snapshots for each route that were re-applied on top of the new tenant smoothing, causing short tenant-level exhaustion.
- Checks run: ingestion replay on staging with merge simulation reproduced 429s; enabling route isolation for the test tenant prevented the 429s.
mitigation_workaround:
1) Apply temporary route isolation for nebulasearch-prod: set per-route quota isolation to true (console -> tenant -> routes -> isolation).
2) Advise customer to stagger orchestrated worker restarts across a 5-minute window rather than all-at-once.
3) Increase tenant burst credit (support-side) by +1000 tokens for 1 hour to smooth immediate load.
4) Rolling restart of rate-limiter pods to clear in-memory snapshots (coordinated with SRE).
next_steps:
- Engineering to create a safe migration path that reconciles route token snapshots with tenant smoothing (owner: eng/rate-limiter team).
- Add post-merge validation to consolidation tool to ensure route and tenant windows are reconciled before enabling traffic.
- SRE to schedule a controlled rollout of a fix and monitor NebulaSearch metrics for 24 hours post patch.
- Customer Success to coordinate operator window for a planned tenant merge next week to validate fix.
resolution_notes: (pending) temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: route isolation enabled and temporary burst credit granted. Early telemetry shows 429 occurrences dropped from ~8/hour to zero during the first 4-hour observation window. Engineering fix in queue (PR reference below).
